newsitem.title: UK: Britain may privatise London tube system - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain may privatise London tube system - paper.

text.p: Britain's Conservative government plans to privatise London's underground railway network if it wins the next general election, the Independent on Sunday newspaper said.

It said a firm commitment to sell off the network, which has 260 stations and total assets worth 13 billion pounds ($22 billion), would figure in the Conservatives' manifesto if the next election was held before May 1.

"It is true that work is at an initial stage in the department on taking forward ideas for securing further private sector involvement in the London Underground system," said a Department of Transport spokesman.

The opposition Labour Party, currently well ahead in the opinion polls, vowed to fight the idea. Labour mounted a long campaign against the recent privatisation of the country's rail network, saying the results so far had been disastrous.

Shadow transport minister Glenda Jackson said the reported plans for selling off the underground, or "tube", was "an attempt to drive the final nail into the coffin of public transport in this country".
Labour sources said the party would focus on the issue in the southeast of England since it believed it would be a vote-winner with the 2.5 million commuters who used the system every day.

The idea of privatising the huge network was first floated by Prime Minister John Major last year, when he said he would like to see if the principle of rail privatisation could be applied to the underground.

The Observer said the Department of Transport was considering options to sell the system to one bidder, privatise its different parts separately and franchise services, or sell off whole lines one by one.
